adjudicated_by: Dave Rae (project owner), by his AskUserQuestion answers in this session: 2026-11-04 'We need to cut this down now but, going forward, would drogon help here?' (answer to the AV-1 question, which led to the 64-character cut, b6aeb8f8a) and 'Accept, file follow-ups (Recommended)' (answer to the residual question); the git author of the series is the owner's account, so this is an owner adjudication recorded by the session, not an independent third party
adjudication_rationale: The preview cut (b6aeb8f8a) is the fix for this PR: the worst case for one request falls from 2.4 GB to about 0.8 GB (779 MiB, fresh process, 1000 grants x 100 decisions x 4096 control characters). The residual (uncapped frozen grants, no per-campaign budget, no route concurrency limit, no shipped memory limit) is accepted at the measured figures. Follow-ups to be filed on the owner's go: a per-grant history read (the campaign GET returning only each grant's latest decision) and a heavy-read concurrency cap. Drogon would help the thread-per-connection slow-reader pinning but not the in-memory response build (httplib can already stream: set_chunked_content_provider), so it is not a prerequisite. The git author is the owner's account, so a literal self-naming check against git authors WILL match; this is an audit trail of the ruling, not a verified control.
summary: DE-ESCALATION from BLOCKING (security-guardian I5(a) derivation) to SHOULD (MEDIUM), by the owner's rulings of 2026-11-04. The preview cut b6aeb8f8a is the fix for this PR and REDUCES the worst case (one cold GET of 1000 grants x 100 decisions x 4096 control characters: 105.0 MB and a fresh-process peak of about 779 MiB, from 371.1 MB and about 2.4 GB). It does not CLOSE the finding, so the disposition is not fixed: the residual (no frozen-grant cap, no per-campaign budget, no route concurrency limit, no shipped memory limit) is accepted at the measured figures and its follow-ups are to be filed on the owner's go; no issue number exists yet. Facts restated unchanged (impact I5, exposure E3); only the band and the disposition change. The epistemic status is not changed. The concurrency half (two concurrent GETs, a slow reader holding a worker) remains reasoned from code, not measured. adjudicated_by: Dave Rae (project owner): on 2026-11-04 he asked that Fable be consulted on 64 versus 128, then directed 'keep 64, record Fable's verdict in the ledger'. Fable (enterprise-architect agent, model fable) returned ENDORSE, confidence high. The git author of the series is the owner's account, so this is an owner decision recorded by the session.
adjudication_rationale: The preview length stays at 64 (kHistoryJustificationPreviewChars, access_review_store.hpp). Fable's reasons: (1) the only functional argument for 128 is the re-record label, and preview length is the wrong lever, since a server-side duplicate flag (full-text equality against the previous history row) is correct at any length and is already the deferred follow-up; (2) the preview is about 20 percent of a response entry (about 320 bytes per entry, about 260 bytes fixed), so it is a second-order memory lever next to the 100-decision window and the grant count; (3) the control-character single-request worst case is 779 MiB measured at 64 against about 1.06 GB scaled at 128, with no shipped memory limit and no concurrency cap. Rework for 128 (re-measure, docs figures, drift test, Gate 8) would buy a partial fix of a NICE-mapped finding. Tradeoff accepted: until the duplicate flag lands, a retry whose justification exceeds 64 characters reads as 'supersedes'; the history rows, the audit rows and the named full-text query remain the evidence. Fable's stated change condition: if the duplicate flag is dropped rather than filed, 128 becomes worth the rework. Fable could not confirm: the MCP twin ratio of about 2.2x, every 128 figure (scaled arithmetic, not measured), the absence of a shipped memory limit (compose grep only), and the introducing commit b6aeb8f8a. It also noted that 'typical justifications are short' and 'half or more exceed 64 characters' are both unmeasured.
summary: Preview length decided: keep 64. The server-side duplicate flag remains deferred and has no issue number yet; it needs the owner's go to file and is the fact that keeps 64 correct.
